html:
The Unangax̂, or Aleuts, are the Indigenous people of the Aleutian Islands and the western Alaska Peninsula, a chain of volcanic islands reaching from Alaska toward Kamchatka; Unangam Tanangin means "the land of the Unangax̂". They hunted sea lions, seals, sea otters and whales from light skin kayaks, the iqyax, and fished some of the roughest seas in the world.

After Vitus Bering's voyage of 1741, Russian fur hunters came to the islands for sea otter pelts. They took hostages and forced Unangax̂ men to hunt for them; violence and disease killed most of the people within a few generations, and many were moved to the Pribilof Islands to hunt fur seals. The islands were part of Russian America until the Alaska Purchase of 1867. In 1942 Japan seized Attu and Kiska, and the US moved almost all Unangax̂ to crowded camps in southeast Alaska, where many died. Their eastern neighbours are the Alutiiq.
